I have now split the sensor in two separate sensors. 

One reports whether the device is online and more detailed information through its attributes. This is a breaking change involving the overall state of the main sensor, that has now been moved to its attributes.

The other sensor reports whether the printer is operating correctly or not.
There are a couple of merge conflicts.
Please link a docs PR in this PR description. We want to add the binary sensor platform to `ha_platforms` front matter.

issue_context.title: Pysyncthru no longer defines SYNCTHRU_STATE_HUMAN
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When using a samsung printer, this error pops up every time the system starts up
```
2021-03-19 09:10:40 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.sensor] syncthru: Error on device update!
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 360, in _async_add_entity
    await entity.async_device_update(warning=False)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 465, in async_device_update
    await task
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/syncthru/sensor.py", line 157, in async_update
    self._state = SYNCTHRU_STATE_HUMAN[self.syncthru.device_status()]
KeyError: <SyncthruState.TESTING: 4>
```
The source code from https://github.com/nielstron/pysyncthru/blob/5856bce9991439c592bcade21f1df3eb7349adb3/pysyncthru/__init__.py shows that SYNCTHRU_STATE_HUMAN[...] no longer exist. It looks like this code shall be updated to use new class

```

class SyncthruState(Enum):
    INVALID = -1  # invalid state for values returned that are not in [1,5]
    OFFLINE = 0
    UNKNOWN = 1
    NORMAL = 2
    WARNING = 3
    TESTING = 4
    ERROR = 5
```

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

Core.2021.3.4

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Samsung Printers with SyncThru web interface

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/syncthru/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
# Put your YAML below this line

```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt

2021-03-19 09:10:40 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.sensor] syncthru: Error on device update!
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 360, in _async_add_entity
    await entity.async_device_update(warning=False)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 465, in async_device_update
    await task
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/syncthru/sensor.py", line 157, in async_update
    self._state = SYNCTHRU_STATE_HUMAN[self.syncthru.device_status()]
KeyError: <SyncthruState.TESTING: 4>

```
comments:
Hey there @nielstron, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`syncthru`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L467) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Thanks for the hint. Something is definitely wrong here, I'll look into it!

The current version of pysyncthru in home assistant is 0.7.0. The corresponding code can be found here: https://github.com/nielstron/pysyncthru/blob/80c1b10df3abc7d9340b4c5d3550e03962b93fb5/pysyncthru/__init__.py

The testing state is simply missing in that version of pysyncthru. There is no quick fix other than manually adjusting the pysyncthru installation in your home assistant to add 
```python
    SyncthruState.TESTING: "testing",
```
However, if my pull request gets accepted and will be merge into the current home-assistant version, the issue should be fixed though.

Or, you manually adjust  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/syncthru/sensor.py", line 157 to
```python
self._state = SYNCTHRU_STATE_HUMAN.get(self.syncthru.device_status(), "Testing")

Thank you for the patch. and sorry for the late response. I saw this today and patched the code directly in the file indicated. It works!
Looking forward for the pull request to be accepted. 
Cheers Ignacio

review_comments: It would be good to set the state attribute keys explicitly here so we can check what they are and their formatting. Can be done in a follow up PR too.
Please exclude this module from coverage calculation in `.coveragerc`.
